Class ProtectionGameTests

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest.ProtectionGameTests
public final class ProtectionGameTests extends Object
The rules that keep a gesture from writing where it should not: build height, entity obstruction, destination consultation, actor-preserving cleanup, and growth checks in simulation and commit.

    • playerStorageSettlementUsesPlayerForCleanup

    • settleKeepsAnEmptyTopBlockWhoseRemovalIsRefused

      @GameTest(structure="somestacks:somestacks_empty", maxTicks=100) public void settleKeepsAnEmptyTopBlockWhoseRemovalIsRefused(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A refused cleanup leaves the empty top Storage block in both the world and the resolved run. To reproduce in-game: protect the top block of a two-block temporary Storage pile from [SomeStacks], leave one item in the bottom block, and trigger settlement. The protected empty top block remains; after allowing [SomeStacks], the next settlement removes it.

    • refusedRemovalStillLetsTheBarsAboveComeDown

      @GameTest(structure="somestacks:somestacks_empty", maxTicks=100) public void refusedRemovalStillLetsTheBarsAboveComeDown(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A refused removal keeps an emptied Bar block without preventing the unsupported block above from collapsing. To reproduce in-game: build a supported two-block Bar column, deny [SomeStacks] permission to remove the lower block, and extract its bottom support. The empty lower block remains, while the unsupported upper block comes down.

    • adjacentDepositsHonorBlockUseCallbacks

      @GameTest(structure="somestacks:somestacks_empty", maxTicks=100) public void adjacentDepositsHonorBlockUseCallbacks(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Destination block-use callbacks can refuse neighboring deposits. To reproduce in-game: deny block use at a stack with a protection mod, then modifier-click its support through an empty cell. No item moves.

    • placementAndAdjacentDepositsUseVanillaAuthority

      @GameTest(structure="somestacks:somestacks_empty", maxTicks=100) public void placementAndAdjacentDepositsUseVanillaAuthority(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce in-game: place a stack against an ordinary block, then modifier-click through empty grounded cells at their support. Placement uses vanilla checks, and neighboring deposits work when destination block-use callbacks permit them.
